The first downloadable build of **Ascending Duel** — a roguelike where you duel your way up
a tower. This is an early prototype: one fight, one opponent, no tower yet.

Download `ascend-duel-v0.1.0-windows-amd64.exe` and run it. Everything is embedded in the
binary; there is nothing to install and nothing to unpack. Windows will warn you about an
unsigned executable, because it is one.

## What you can do

You are dealt a hand of eight cards from a 30-card deck and spend an action-point budget on
up to five of them. Click a card to select it, drag it along the row to reorder, then press
**DUEL!**. **Discard** throws the selected cards back instead, four times a round. **Deck**
shows everything you own.

Six concepts, each in five elements — plain, fire, ice, lightning and earth:

| Category | Card | AP | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| setup | Prepare | 1 | Banks +2 AP for the next round |
| setup | Guard | 3 | Halves every attack in the opponent's next turn |
| attack | Strike | 2 | Damage equal to your Strength |
| attack | Heavy | 4 | Double Strength |
| defend | Dodge | 2 | Negates the first incoming attack |
| defend | Riposte | 3 | Negates the first incoming attack and hits back |

A round resolves as **a whole turn each**: everything you queued goes off in category order
— setups, then attacks, then defenses — and only then does the enemy act. Your defenses
therefore go up before their blows land. Elements are colour only so far; they do nothing
yet.

## What is missing

Everything above the first fight. There is no tower, no run structure, no rings or brands,
no deckbuilding between fights, and one enemy who always opens with the same two attacks —
which two defensive cards will shut out completely. The art is placeholder.

## Known

Unsigned binary, so SmartScreen will object. Windows x64 only.
